payload.text: Molt 1.4.6 rollout, started 9 Nov on hv's word, coordinated by rhadamanth-sysadm. Tap verified: remote and local clone at 94e58f54 'molt 1.4.6', Formula/molt.rb pins tag v1.4.6 at revision f2d2627670208c73d92ae3efb5ad559f5d50fe77. Per sleeve: 'brew upgrade molt', then 'molt --version' reads 'molt 1.4.6 (brew, f2d2627670208c73d92ae3efb5ad559f5d50fe77)'; 'molt use brew' only if that line does not say brew (rhadamanth has no ~/.local/bin/molt and gyges is brew-only, so it should be unnecessary on both). STATE: gyges dispatched; rhadamanth HELD while the heavy lane carries AE's devvm release and webber-dc's build loop, on hv's no-brew-during-a-suite rule, released on hv's word or when the lane clears; kovacs not started and not a plain brew upgrade. FIRST REAL PROOF of 1.4.6, independent of Molt's own suite: AE's devvm release 2 amd64 image, built from the tap 20 minutes after the cut, ran molt doctor in a login shell on WSL2 at 1.4.6 (brew, f2d262767020) and passed, exit 0, 06:48Z. It proves 0099 is inert where there is no profile ('Checking sandbox profile... none needed, and none of molt's here', and the managed floor the same), and incidentally proves 0094 (font: 'Windows draws this terminal'), 0095 (external dependencies 'envsubst' alone, no bats) and 0097 (new-user --from built the stack). Doctor's closing line was the bare 'All checks passed.' at log line 76, confirming the unprefixed echo in a real run. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: the migration path. kovacs is the only sleeve holding Molt's AppArmor profile, so it alone exercises the resleeve that moves the sidecar and Ubuntu's copy into /var/lib/molt/apparmor and reports 'Moved: <old> -> <new>'; until then molt doctor's sandbox check fails naming both. That is 0099's owed proof and hv's own leg: hv runs molt upgrade from a plain terminal with Claude Code quit (kovacs-sysadm must stop first, since the move fails while any claude process runs), kovacs-sysadm then checks only Molt's bwrap-userns-restrict is in /etc/apparmor.d with both files under /var/lib/molt/apparmor and molt doctor passing, then on hv's go 'sudo systemctl reset-failed apparmor && sudo systemctl restart apparmor' and sends systemctl status apparmor. Until that lands, any reboot or apparmor restart lets the distro's unpriv_bwrap win again; 'sudo apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict' repairs it.
